t19: This content is for readers 18 and older. It is for informational and entertainment purposes; it is not advice about betting, alcohol consumption, or similar topics.
t20: Truth or Dare is the easiest party game to set up; but without a good question list, it runs dry in three rounds. Below is a tiered list and a few rules that keep the game alive.
t22: What's the most innocent lie you've kept hidden so far?
t23: What are the three apps you use most on your phone?
t24: Whose advice in this group do you trust the most?
t25: Which TV show do you think is most overrated?
t26: Did you regret a purchase you made in the last month?
t28: Who in this group do you think you're most like?
t29: If you could gain one skill overnight, what would it be?
t30: When did you last need to apologize but didn't?
t31: Is there a habit about yourself you'd like to change?
t33: Speak only in song lyrics for one minute.
t34: Do an impersonation of someone in the group.
t35: Describe your phone's last photo without looking at the gallery.
t36: Stay straight-faced for one minute without laughing.
t38: Spend the next round standing on one leg.
t39: Sing a 30-second improvised song to someone in the group.
t40: Explain a movie using only facial expressions until someone gets it.
t41: Start every sentence for the next two rounds with "in my opinion".
t42: 4 rules that keep the game alive
t44: Everyone gets one pass; forcing the game kills it.
t45: Don't pick the same person twice in a row.
t50: When there's a score, the game stays taken seriously even later in the night.
t51: Letting a spinner decide turn order and difficulty
t52: When people decide who plays and how hard the task is, debate breaks out. In Shot Spinner, the spinner sets both the turn order and difficulty level, picks a random task from the pool, and handles the score automatically. That way you focus on playing instead of managing the game.
t54: How many people play Truth or Dare?
t55: You can play with a minimum of 3, but it's much more fun in groups of 5–10. In a large group, shorten round time to speed up waits.
t56: How do you prevent uncomfortable questions?
t57: Discuss boundaries at the start and give everyone a pass. Using a ready-made question pool prevents made-up cruel questions on the spot.
t59: Not necessary, but recommended. Games with a scoreboard keep getting attention later in the night.
t61: Spin the spinner, take a task by difficulty level, earn points or take a shot.
